US2Y.source: latest U.S. close before Labor Day holiday

learning_v2.note: No ACTIONABLE v2 context-aware segment was identified that justified a material confidence change; current escalation facts and contemporaneous oil/USD context dominate.

predictions.mechanism: A direct warning that ships near Khasab face strike risk raises the probability of immediate shipping disruption and increases geopolitical safe-haven demand.
predictions.invalidation: Iran retracts the warning, tanker traffic normalizes, and no further military incidents occur near the Hormuz approaches.

predictions.mechanism: Higher shipping and oil-risk premia worsen the energy-cost backdrop for Germany's industrial economy and favor risk-off positioning.
predictions.invalidation: Brent falls sharply as shipping normalizes or a credible de-escalation agreement is announced.

predictions.mechanism: Escalating shipping risk around Hormuz raises imported-energy costs and geopolitical risk premia across euro-area equities.
predictions.invalidation: Hormuz transit normalizes and oil gives back the risk premium.

predictions.mechanism: Silver gets some safe-haven and softer-dollar support, but its industrial sensitivity makes the signal weaker than gold.
predictions.invalidation: Risk premia fade quickly or the dollar rebounds materially.

predictions.mechanism: French equities are exposed to broader European risk-off sentiment and higher imported energy costs, though less directly than Germany.
predictions.invalidation: European risk sentiment improves materially alongside lower oil prices.

predictions.mechanism: Japan's dependence on imported energy makes a sustained Hormuz shipping premium a negative input-cost shock, while risk-off demand can strengthen the yen and pressure exporters.
predictions.invalidation: Oil prices retreat and regional risk sentiment recovers decisively.
